INIT: User prompt 1 explains its idea, its intent, its project.

I. Intent clarification loop sub-workflow
Goal of this step: Is the intent clear, coherent, consistent and coherent just by itself?
INPUT: The user's prompt
1. AI processes the prompt, captures the clear intention items and transforms the items in intent candidates
2. AI comes back with questions using the question tool with clarification questions. 
Note: This intent clarification should identify the invariants that will allow you to understand the definition of the project 
and allow you to minimize the amount of questions you'll have to ask to the user. 
3. AI captures answers and asks questions until it's intent is clear. 
4. AI formulates clear, explicit, coherent intent candidates
5. JEV  (+Haiku/Sonnet) Judge sequence that gates the output. 
6. Fix loop until only low findings remain. 

OUTPUT/OUTCOME: One or several validated, clear, explicit, consistent, coherent intent candidates 

II. Intent integration sub-workflow
Goal of this step: How can we integrate those valid, clarified intents into the current system? 
INPUT: Intent candidates 

1. AI checks coherence between new intent and available intent and SR items. 
If incoherences, come back to the user with questions, eventually spawning study room.
The goal of those questions and study is to clarify the invariants of the projects that will allow you to answer to most of the questions you could have.
3. User and AI reach common understanding and agreement on SR/architecture update to integrate new intent.  
4. AI identifies and proposes SRs/Intent to update/create/delete
5. JEV  (+Haiku/Sonnet) Judge confirms the proposal. 
6. Fix loop until only low findings remain. 

OUTPUT/OUTCOME: Intent is confirmed to be integrateable through a validated plan of updates. 

Note: I'm not sure whether I and II. should actually be merged. 
Perhaps it would make more sense to make it as only one step to reduce time of execution and catch incompatibilities early. We can discuss that.

III. SR artifacts update sub-workflow

1. AI executes the plan of updates.
2. Staleness is computed. 
3. specs and or implementation plan are written if necessary to update code and test based on staleness. 
New SRs are considered new so are also taken into account to write specs / implementation plans.
3. AI reviews the new documents against intent, SRs and staleness, code feasability... 
Note that you should also leverage superpowers plan review skills
4. AI fixes the findings until only low findings remain.

OUTPUT/OUTCOME: Reviewed and Validated set of implementation plans to execute

IV. Execute development spec/plan 
INPUT: All artifacts from plumb
1.Develop/review/fix loop workflow against plumb's artifacts. 
2. Present proof of updated come proving intent has been successfully integrated into the system. 
OUTPUT/OUTCOME: PROOF OF INTENT

Notes: 
- the modality on how this workflow should be executed should support interactivity 
as in it shouldnt be a black boxed workflow and leverage coding agent orchestration features like claude code workflow, hooks..

- Proof of intent should also be specified by the user and supported by the system. 
This should remain flexible in terms of definition of proof and code supporting the proof should be also planned.

- As you know there's already a lot of artifacts in plumb. I need you to evaluate whether we should create a new version of the repo
Or perhaps just simplify/delete most of the requirements to come up with a more streamlined list of artifacts? 
I fear that there are actually many duplicates, or that the actual definition of an SR is actually blur currently in the plumb project.

- I need you to articulate the current sessions to come up with a common strategy in order to simplify and rationalize the execution of this new 
rationalization of the workflows. There are a few branches on-going, we need to figure out what to keep, what to drop, and how to proceed with clean up and progress.
</pasted_content id="14a1">
